summary.headline: Simplex Castings FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 18% to Rs 202 crore and PAT 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore; FY27 target Rs 300 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue up about 18% to Rs 202 crore, EBITDA up 20% to Rs 37.39 crore with margin expansion, and PAT up 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore. Q4 revenue was slightly below the prior-year Q4 (about Rs 67 crore cited by an analyst), which management attributed to customer site delays and LPG/gas supply disruptions that held back dispatches. The company received RDSO approval to restart wagon bogie manufacturing, with cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month now built. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs 300 crore and a FY28 aspiration of Rs 500 crore, contingent on execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders.

segments.name: Railways (cast and fabricated bogies)
segments.commentary: RDSO approval received to restart wagon bogies; 200-250 cast bogies a month capacity built. Cast bogie sale value about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Developmental order for fabricated loco bogies; FY27 target Rs 50 crore from cast railway business.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Management targets about Rs 50 crore from power in FY27, linked to BHEL and L&T orders for 32 and 16 coal-based thermal plants to be commissioned by 2032.

segments.name: Steel (coke oven doors and castings)
segments.commentary: Coke oven door segment estimated at Rs 50-60 crore of about Rs 200-220 crore revenue; management claims about 70% share of India's coke oven doors and expects growth toward Rs 100 crore over 2-3 years. Recent orders from SMS and Thyssen for SAIL stamp-charging batteries.

segments.name: Defence and shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Supplies A-brackets, B-brackets and stern boss castings to shipyards and components to Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur (Dhanush). Management says margins above 10% but segment, with other rest-of-business, expected at only 15-20% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target Rs 300 crore: about Rs 200 crore from existing business (stated as already closed), Rs 50 crore from cast railway business and about Rs 50 crore from power.
FY27 margins guided similar to FY26; cost-reduction gains expected to show in Q3-Q4 FY27.
EBITDA/PAT margin floor of 8-10% reiterated as minimum goal.
FY28 revenue aspiration of about Rs 500 crore, dependent on execution, acquisition and EPC, and railway orders.
FY27 capex planned at Rs 25 crore.
Expects an order of 100-200 bogies within about a month and consistent 200-bogie production from September onwards.
capex_capacity: Cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month built under the first preferential issue; in CWIP until commercial production and prototype/first order.
Second preferential issue of about Rs 50 crore; about half earmarked for fabricated bogie facilities (Rs 25 crore capital and Rs 25 crore working capital).
FY27 capex target Rs 25 crore; FY26 capex about Rs 15 crore.
Spare land available at both Bhilai and Rajnandgaon units for expansion and semi-mechanisation.
Centrifugal rolls project (Rs 1.5-2 crore investment) dropped after market survey.
demand_pricing: Wagon bogies: wagon makers about 70-75% of market and railways spares about 20-25%; management targets both channels.
Possible wagon mega-order: management estimates 6,000 bogies (about 2 tonnes cast weight each) for 8,000-10,000 wagons over 3 years, with 20-30% typically outsourced.

Coke oven doors: India has an estimated 150-180 batteries; replacement demand about 3-4% a year; order flow of 2-3 batteries a year, plus about 70-80 batteries for planned 140 million tonne capacity expansion by 2030-2040.
Power and steel demand strong; management says it has become choosy on orders.
Gas (LPG) supply disruptions hit fabrication plants and top line in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue fall YoY versus last Q4 (about Rs 67 crore), and what drove margins higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dispatches slipped because customer site activity was delayed, leaving finished goods inventory that was expected to be realised in April-May. Gas (LPG) shortages also hit fabrication plants. Management said the margin goal is at least 8-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company supply full bogies or only parts, and what is the realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The company assembles bogies from its own castings plus outsourced springs, side bearers, brakes and pads. Cast bogie sale value is about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Couplers and draft gears are planned later.

qa_highlights.question: When will orders from RDSO approval arrive and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: An order of 100-200 bogies is expected in about a month. No further capex is needed for the cast bogie line; it is awaiting the prototype and first order.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 targets, margins, acquisitions and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue target is Rs 300 crore, with margins similar to FY26. Two acquisition talks remain open after one failed; they are in the same line of business. FY27 capex is Rs 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coke oven door market size and share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 150-180 batteries in India, 3-4% annual replacement, and about 70% market share. Coke oven doors are about Rs 50-60 crore of revenue, with growth to about Rs 100 crore expected over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 Rs 500 crore target risk and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Risks are execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders. Management said acquisitions in India had prohibitive multiples, so it is looking abroad in steel, power or railways, size about Rs 20-100 crore. Funding may come from debt or equity; the second preferential issue is a Rs 50 crore part of that.

risks_watch: Execution capacity and workforce availability; management plans to skill local labour and mechanise.
Gas/LPG supply and steel price volatility disrupting fabrication and dispatches.
Customer site delays pushing dispatches and inventory across quarters.
Funding for the fabricated bogie and FY28 plan; the second preferential issue (about Rs 50 crore) may need to be supplemented by debt or equity.
Acquisition pipeline: one deal failed on valuations; two remain open with unclear size and funding.
Dependence on the wagon mega-order and RDSO-approved bogie orders for the FY27 railway contribution.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order pipeline across railways, steel and power, but cautious on Q4 dispatches and execution, which management repeatedly called the key challenge. Answers on acquisitions and funding were tentative, with no firm size or funding plan.
key_quotes: So, we are going back to the same market, looking at 70 -75% from the wagon manufacturers and 20-25% from railways directly for spares.
Execution is the challenge. So let us focus on execution.
At least for the next 3-4 years, I am expecting every integrated steel plant, if they are not buying from China, if they are buying from India, the coke oven doors will go from some place.
Of all the coke oven doors that are being manufactured in India, 70% is coming from Simplex Castings.
